text:
marie: FYI I'm seeing ~40 pods Pending in ap-southeast1 with GPU requests. Scheduler log shows repeated FailedScheduling -> affinity/anti-affinity conflicts and then autoscaler coldstarts. Cost jump this morning.
aj: ugh. are they tiny jobs or long-running?
marie: mostly short inference workers (1-3m) but they request gpu=1 and have a hard anti-affinity label: "pod-lattice=true" to avoid co-locating from an old deployment rule.
keith: that anti-affinity sounds like the lattice everybody added last year. It prevents co-locating any two with that label, so packability is terrible.
sam: can you paste the scheduler message?
marie: sure: ```FailedScheduling: 0/50 nodes are available: 42 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity, 8 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.```
nora: ops-bot posted autoscaler events too: "launched 6 instances (gpu-pool-apse1) at 03:12, terminated 5 at 03:14 — scale-down due to low utilization".
marie: exactly — we spin up GPUs to satisfy the hard anti-affinity but jobs finish before they're used, causing churn and cost.
aj: is this only ap-southeast1?
marie: mostly there, region is smaller so fragmentation worse. saw similar pattern in eu-west but less severe.
keith: two levers: relax anti-affinity to soft (preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution) or add a tiny warmpool/reserved set for short inferencers.
sam: we have Optimize recommendations suggesting batching + soft affinity for this workload. But teams haven't applied them.
marie: short-term proposal: patch scheduler config for a placement hint to allow 2 of these pods per GPU node (label-based override), and add a 1-hour cooldown on scale-down for gpu-warmpool.
nora: would that break any tenants that explicitly wanted strict isolation?
keith: might — need to scope by label: only pods with "team=public-infer" and "pod-lattice=true" get the override.
aj: better: flip rule server-side by injecting `affinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` via mutating webhook for that namespace so users don't have to change code.
sam: webhook approach seems lower friction. we need a rollback plan: revert webhook and drain nodes allocated with the policy.
marie: I can prototype webhook to replace hard anti-affinity with a preferred weight 50. Also will add a monitoring alert on Pending pods > 20 for 10m.
nora: I'll tweak autoscaler: increase scale-down-delay for gpu pool to 10m and add an annotation so cost team knows which nodes were reserved.
keith: runbook note: if fragmentation persists, we can enable small-binpacking heuristic in scheduler that prefers filling existing GPU nodes before launching new ones.
aj: need risk review — softening isolation might expose noisy-neighbor risks. Ops: what telemetry do we have for cross-pod GPU interference?
sam: we have nvml metrics and tail-latency traces per token; I'll chart for the affected namespace over last 24h and post.
marie: action items: 1) marie -> prototype mutating webhook (pref affinity) 2) nora -> set autoscaler scale-down delay for gpu pool 3) sam -> perf chart for noisy-neighbor risk 4) keith -> draft scheduler heuristic change PR.
keith: ack, will also add a Canary in ap-southeast1 before global roll.
ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance window 03:30-04:00 UTC for infra upgrades. avoid risky deploys during that time.
marie: ok will schedule webhook rollout after maintenance. posting updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
